parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure Node.js ESM `.mjs` files in `/output`, no external dependencies, manual `process.argv` parsing, Python-like formatting, NetworkX graph behavior, and exact CLI/output matching.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent retained implementation and verification ownership but spawned a child, which spawned a nested helper. The child also implemented directly in `/output`, creating overlapping ownership of the entry deliverable.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a hierarchical graph/CLI/algorithm/format module set, while the child later wrote a flat alternate module set and `/output/test10.mjs`. The parent removed the alternate files and restored its hierarchy.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Final integration was parent-led after a collision: it detected the competing active output tree, deleted child-owned flat files, ensured only its hierarchy remained, and delivered the restored `test10.mjs` artifact.
parallel.verification: The parent compared Node output to the executable on normal, parser, duplicate-node, self-loop, and representative cases after cleanup; the official evaluator then passed 160/160.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final required behavior remained incorrect, but the parallel process temporarily had an overwritten active entrypoint that returned the wrong connectivity value until the parent cleaned it up.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, `.mjs`, no-external-dependency, manual CLI, local module hierarchy, exact formatting, and NetworkX behavior requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single owner: probe executable behavior, build graph/algorithm/format/CLI modules, patch connectivity defects, and validate end to end without delegation.
serial.implementation: Created one flat module hierarchy with graph, CLI, formatting, traversal, shortest paths, MST, connectivity, index exports, and the `test10.mjs` entry file.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Integrated locally in the same workspace with no competing writers; final file inventory matched the single selected implementation hierarchy.
serial.verification: Ran executable-vs-Node checks for normal cases, duplicate/equality patterns, parser errors, and a representative equality-pattern sweep that ended with `OK`; official evaluation passed 160/160.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final required behavior remained incorrect; earlier connectivity mismatches were found and patched before final delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the ESM, manual CLI, no external dependency, `.mjs`, and exact NetworkX behavior requirements from the prompt.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and also inspected the provided source file plus executable behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material final requirement-coverage difference; both covered the required output behavior and both passed official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across parent, first child, and nested child, but parent and first child both implemented into `/output`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner for probing, implementation, corrections, verification, and final inventory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had overlapping implementation ownership; serial had one coherent owner and no concurrent implementation collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The visible parallel handoff did not establish a stable file-ownership boundary, and the child wrote a different entrypoint and library layout into the shared output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial began from an empty `/output` and then wrote one implementation tree without cross-agent interface boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel needed implicit reconciliation between independent implementations; serial avoided that interface problem by having no cross-agent file contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent built a hierarchical graph/algorithm/CLI implementation and later restored it after the child's flat implementation appeared.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a flat but coherent implementation and fixed the `node_connectivity` algorithm through two observed mismatch families.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation paths reached correct behavior, but parallel had two competing implementations while serial iterated within one tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child and nested child completed, the child result reached the parent, and the parent rejected the child-written implementation through cleanup rather than blindly joining it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local findings flowed directly into patches and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result reception and rejection step; serial had only local iteration.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had a concrete shared-output conflict: the active deliverable was replaced by the child and then removed/restored by the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified `/output` was empty before writing and later inventoried a single final module tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred a shared-state recovery episode; serial had no shared-state contention.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed many executable-vs-Node comparisons after cleanup and the official evaluator passed all 160 samples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial patched connectivity based on mismatches, completed a representative equality-pattern and CLI sweep with `OK`, and passed all 160 official samples.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached strong acceptance evidence; parallel's verification also served to catch and recover from the overwritten active entrypoint.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used three subagents and more total tool/LLM activity but completed without timeout and delivered after parent cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, took longer wall-clock agent time, and closed after a representative verification sweep.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's extra budget went partly to concurrent duplicated work and cleanup; serial spent more single-thread time on verification but avoided concurrency recovery.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both completed evaluations passed 160 of 160. The task-solving difference is process-level. Parallel gained concurrent probing/implementation but introduced a shared-output deliverable overwrite that the parent detected and corrected before final delivery. Serial solved the same obligations in one ownership stream, found and patched ordinary connectivity bugs, and did not need collision recovery.
parallel_contributors: Concurrent child work produced extra probing and an alternate implementation, but the useful final deliverable came from the parent after cleanup.
The retained deliverable-overwrite episode was adverse process overhead, not an official failure contributor because it was corrected before final evaluation.
serial_contributors: Single-owner implementation avoided shared-output collisions and supported a straightforward patch-and-verify loop.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial run initially overcounted `node_connectivity` on duplicate/self-loop patterns and fixed it locally; the parallel parent also handled parser and connectivity edge cases but additionally had to recover from a child-written alternate tree.

The final module layouts differed: parallel delivered a hierarchical `lib/cli`, `lib/graph`, `lib/algorithms`, `lib/format` hierarchy while serial delivered flatter `lib/*.mjs` modules plus algorithm modules.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the retained pattern is an evidenced parallel adverse process episode corrected before official evaluation

The parent created and began testing the required `/output/test10.mjs` deliverable, then a live child independently applied a patch that added its own `/output/test10.mjs` and flat library tree. The parent later observed that another agent had written a different implementation into `/output`, saw the active entrypoint produce the wrong connectivity result on a probed case, and removed the child files before final verification. That is a child action replacing the directly executed deliverable while another actor owned and used it.
candidates.realized_consequence: The parallel parent had to stop normal verification, diagnose that the active entrypoint came from a different implementation, delete the child-owned files, restore its own `/output/test10.mjs`, and repeat verification before closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The same entry file was involved, but because the object overwritten was the required executable entry source, Deliverable Overwrite is the more specific canonical label.
